subject: Post-call: Prompt collection & model-fit next steps (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Morris <evan.morris@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Prompt collection & model-fit next steps (Acme Corp)

Hi Evan / Sofia —

Thanks for the time today — great conversation on the ingestion pipeline and the main user flows for your customer support summarization feature. Per the call, here's a short recap and the asks so we can move the model-fit eval forward: 

What Redwood will do: 
- Share recommended model candidates and lightweight benchmark results for Acme's dataset characteristics. See initial benchmark link below.
- Run an eval on the prompt set you provide (we'll synthetic-augment if needed for edge cases).
- Produce a quality regression report and suggested quantization profile if you want a cost vs latency tradeoff.

What we need from you: 
1) A prompt collection CSV (one prompt per row) that includes a small label column indicating expected output type (summary, action-item, sentiment). If prompts include PII, please follow the attached redaction guidance.
2) Examples of edge cases (long threads, mixed languages, heavy code snippets).
3) Any hard constraints (max latency SLO, token limits, or specific hallucination tolerances).

Recommended models (initial): rwd-3b-q, rwd-7b-q, and rwd-14b-std. We'll prioritize rwd-7b-q based on call notes (70% of requests are ~600 tokens). Full performance matrix: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/acme-eval-2026

Attachments: acme_prompt_examples.csv (template), redaction_guidelines.pdf

Proposed next steps:
- Evan: share the prompt CSV + edge cases by EOD Friday (2026-06-12).
- We'll queue an eval (3 business days) and share a draft report and model recommendation.

If you want, I can loop in one of our SREs for a short architecture sync once the prompts are in.

Thanks again — looking forward to the prompt set.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Evan Morris <evan.morris@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt collection & model-fit next steps (Acme Corp)

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the template. Quick answers:
- We'll attach an initial set of ~120 prompts (mixture of summaries and action-item extraction) — see attached CSV.
- PII: we can provide a redacted set. Our legal prefers automated token-level redaction; happy to follow Redwood's guidance if you share the doc.
- Edge cases: will flag ~15 threads with long context and a couple with code snippets.

Timeline: we'll try to get this to you by Friday (2026-06-12). If that slips, we can do Monday next week.

Attaching: acme_prompt_examples.csv

Thanks,
Evan Morris
Product Manager, Acme Corp
evan.morris@acme.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Evan Morris <evan.morris@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt collection & model-fit next steps (Acme Corp)

Evan / Marissa —

Thanks for the examples, Evan. A couple of quick notes from the infra/eval side: 
- For the initial run, 120 prompts is a good start; ideally we get 300-500 to see distributional issues. If that's hard, we can augment via synthetic variations.
- Redaction: if you can provide a redacted CSV plus a mapping file (local IDs only) that keeps examples realistic without PII, that's perfect. If you need our redaction tool, we can run a one-off redaction and return a mapping.
- Metrics we'll report: ROUGE-L and our hallucination delta (fraction of responses with invented entities vs ground truth). We'll also include per-prompt latency percentiles.
- Recommended eval configs: run rwd-7b-q at fp16 quantization and a baseline rwd-3b-q for cost comparison. If latency is critical, we'll add a rwd-3b-q low-latency profile.

Quick ask: can you flag any legal/contractual constraints on sharing even redacted content? We'll need to know if the data can be processed in our hosted environment vs Dedicated/Private.

- Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Morris <evan.morris@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt collection & model-fit next steps (Acme Corp)

Evan —

Appreciate the quick turn. That plan works. A few small additions: 
- Please include a one-line column that marks whether the example is production-facing (yes/no). That helps prioritize the eval.
- If you can't share redacted mappings, send an explicit note here stating the data cannot leave Acme systems; we'll route to our Dedicated/Private team and provide a scoped MSA addendum if needed.
- We'll attach our redaction_guidelines.pdf and a sample evaluation spreadsheet — I added the shared sheet link above.

Next steps (confirmed):
1) Evan: upload prompt CSV + edge-case examples + production-flag column by EOD 2026-06-12.
2) Redwood: commence eval within 1 business day of receiving data and share preliminary report in ~3 business days.

If anything changes on your end, ping me and we'll adjust.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
